chapter_title: Chương 169: Cha Trở Nên Sành Điệu

segments.title: Chương 169: Cha Trở Nên Sành Điệu
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang left Modu but didn't fly to Rongcheng immediately. Instead, he came to Jinling, the ancient capital of six dynasties.

There, he had a startup partner from his previous life.

To be precise, it was the big brother who had led him into the world of startups. It was unknown how capable he was now, being relatively young, but his character was absolutely solid.

The reason he was only looking for him now was that he didn't have his contact information.

Game Science was still in need of a chief steward.

Chen Guiliang took a taxi to the old Hehuatang district of Jinling, asking for directions along the way based on his vague memory.

In his past life, he had only been here once, as a guest at his big brother's home.

Nestled in the messy, old, and narrow alleys was a small shop selling salted duck.

A fly repellent spun slowly, its red silk ribbons driving away the flies that tried to get close to the duck meat. The weather was muggy and hot, and there was hardly anyone in the alley. The shop owner was lying inside, napping under a fan.

"Hello, may I ask if Qu Guohao is here?" Chen Guiliang asked.

After calling out twice, the owner finally woke up. "What are you looking for him for?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I'm his friend."

"Come in, have a seat," the owner said, then tilted his head back and shouted upstairs, "Guohao, your friend is here!"

Chen Guiliang walked in carrying some fruit. "Uncle, a small gift. It's just a small token."

"You came all this way, no need to bring gifts," the owner said with a broad smile.

A young man of about twenty-five or twenty-six, wearing a tank top, came downstairs. He found Chen Guiliang a bit familiar. "You are..."

"Chen Guiliang," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

"Holy crap!"

Qu Guohao rubbed his eyes. "No wonder you looked so familiar. I just saw news about you last month. What brings you to my house?"

Chen Guiliang said, "My company has been recruiting recently, and someone recommended you. So, I flew here from Jingcheng specifically, to learn from Liu Bei's three visits to the thatched cottage."

Qu Guohao felt a little pleased that he could actually attract a visit from a new internet tycoon for a job offer. At the same time, he was a bit embarrassed, as he was at the lowest point of his life.

The owner brought over a cup of tea and aimed the electric fan at Chen Guiliang.

In 1999, a super-elite startup team was formed, consisting of five Harvard MBAs and two Chicago MBAs.

They drafted their business plan in May, secured 47 million USD in investment in June, returned to China to set up the company in July, launched their website in November, and reached 4.5 million registered users by December.

In one year, the company's staff expanded to 300 people, and they burned through 3 million USD on advertising alone.

This company was called Yitang.

At the time, Qu Guohao was a student union leader at Nanjing University and met Yitang's criteria for expansion, so he became a student employee and the head of promotions at the university. After graduating, he officially joined Yitang and became a key member in the Jinling region.

After a few years, Yitang had burned through all 47 million USD.

The company was laying people off every year. Qu Guohao's position was continually promoted, yet his salary actually decreased. When the layoff rate exceeded 90%, Qu Guohao, along with the entire branch office, was let go.

He was now cooped up at home, studying to retake the graduate school entrance exams.

Qu Guohao lamented, "Sigh, I really did a good job at Yitang before, otherwise I wouldn't have only been laid off this year. I didn't expect someone to still remember me and recommend me to ByteDance. Was it an old colleague from Yitang who recommended me?"

"Perhaps, I'm not sure either," Chen Guiliang asked, "Yitang is probably about to go under. Why do you think they failed?"

Qu Guohao smiled and said, "The upper management were all overseas returnees. Their heads were filled with American thinking. They tried to force the American internet company model onto China. Moreover, these returnee executives were severely out of touch with us local employees. Do you know what they used to say?"

"What did they say?" Chen Guiliang played along.

Qu Guohao said sarcastically, "The founder said that China's internet technology was five years behind the West, and China's management techniques were at least twenty years behind. He looked down on his company's local employees, even looking down on the very place where he started his business. The localization proposals my colleagues and I submitted disappeared like stones into the sea, one after another. I don't even know if those executives ever read them."

"Do you know anything about the online gaming industry?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Qu Guohao shook his head. "I don't play games."

In our last life, you were the one who led us into gaming, and now you're fucking telling me you don't play games? Chen Guiliang said, "I have a gaming company, and I'd like to invite you to take on a management role."

"Not ByteDance?" Qu Guohao was quite surprised.

Chen Guiliang said, "ByteDance is fully staffed. Game Science is still short of professional talent. If you were to be parachuted in directly, it would be difficult to win over the team. If you're willing to join, you'll need to prove your abilities."

Qu Guohao thought for a moment and asked, "What do you want me to do?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Through the interest groups on Xiaonei, we've already contacted some university fans of Legends of the Three Kingdoms. They applied last semester and are about to establish board game societies at their respective schools."

"Your first task is to familiarize yourself with the Legends of the Three Kingdoms business as quickly as possible. Your second task, after the school year begins, is to get in touch with the board game societies at each university and have them maintain regular communication. Your third task is to organize the first offline Legends of the Three Kingdoms university league during the National Day holiday. This year, we'll only have three competition zones: Jingcheng, Modu, and Yangcheng."

"Next year, we'll expand to Rongcheng, Jinling, and Jiangcheng."

Qu Guohao said, "As long as the funding is sufficient, there's no problem at all. Yitang has been on life support for the past few years, with fewer and fewer employees and funds. I don't have any other skills, but I can get the job done for you with the least amount of money and manpower."

"That's a very impressive skill," Chen Guiliang said.

Qu Guohao smiled bitterly. "It was forged out of necessity. Yitang was constantly laying people off, yet they didn't provide enough funding and still wanted you to organize events and do promotions. You had no choice but to do the work of ten people by yourself."

Qu Guohao didn't ask about the salary, but Chen Guiliang proactively offered him a monthly salary of 6000. He also promised that as long as the Legends of the Three Kingdoms university league was done well, he would give Qu Guohao a promotion and a raise, making him the general manager of Game Science directly.

At noon, Chen Guiliang stayed for a meal at Qu Guohao's home.

When his parents learned that Chen Guiliang was a company owner who had come specially to hire their son, they were very enthusiastic and bought a large pile of delicious food to treat him.

In the late morning, Chen Guiliang took his leave.

Qu Guohao packed his luggage, preparing to head to Jingcheng for work.

He had three startup partners in his previous life. Chen Guiliang only planned to contact Qu Guohao and couldn't be bothered to approach the other two.

Because as for the remaining two: one had poor character, someone you could share hardship with but not wealth. The other had a poor personality, giving up at the first sign of a setback, and then just lying flat once he achieved financial freedom.

Hmm, the one with the poor personality often took Chen Guiliang to find "little sisters," severely dampening our young hero Chen's fighting spirit!

In mid-July, Chen Guiliang returned to his hometown.

He first took some new clothes and shoes to his maternal grandmother's house.

The old folks were reluctant to spend money. Giving them cash would just be saved, so it was better to buy them things directly.

His young uncle was beaming, his beard shaved clean, and his clothes were tidier than before.

He was holding a three-year-old little girl. This was the daughter he had gained, and he doted on her as if she were his own. The little girl lay in his arms, looking at Chen Guiliang curiously.

His young uncle pointed to the woman beside him and said, "This is your aunt, Xiao Ju. We just got our marriage certificate a few days ago."

"Hello, Aunt," Chen Guiliang greeted her.

Xiao Ju enthusiastically welcomed him. "Quick, come in and sit. It's so hot outside."

Chen Guiliang sat down in the main room. Xiao Ju went to make tea, then went to the kitchen to wash tomatoes for him.

He glanced at the floor; it was swept very clean, and things in the room were no longer scattered about like before.

His maternal grandmother said in a low voice, "Your young aunt is very good, honest and hardworking."

His maternal grandfather sat nearby, smiling.

His young uncle said, "About that thirty thousand yuan I borrowed from you, I'll pay some back each year. I'll go out to work next year."

The thirty thousand yuan was for the bride price.

This was clearly too much. In the rural areas of Longdu City, eight or ten thousand would have been fine under normal circumstances, and many didn't ask for a bride price at all. Not to mention, she was a remarried widow.

But his young uncle's situation was also special. He had a slight limp in one foot, making it difficult to find a wife in the countryside.

That thirty thousand yuan had all been left with Xiao Ju's deceased husband's family. After paying off his medical debts, only two or three thousand remained.

"Forget about going out to work. It's not easy to earn money out there," Chen Guiliang said. "Weren't you looking after and raising fish for people before? I'll lend you some more money to contract a fish pond. It's okay if you lose money; you can pay it back slowly. As long as your luck isn't too bad, it can be a side business."

His young uncle didn't know what he could do if he went out to work. Hearing Chen Guiliang's proposal, he said, "Then I'll raise fish. Seventh Guan doesn't want to do it anymore. I'll take over his fish pond."

This Seventh Guan, after a few twists and turns in kinship, was actually Chen Guiliang's distant great-grand-uncle.

Their daughter was married far away, and their son had settled in the city. The old couple usually farmed, ran a boat, and raised fish. They were getting old in recent years and didn't want to contract the village's fish pond anymore. They even planned to sell their cargo boat. The boat business was mostly just for hauling fertilizer for the villagers and transporting grain during tax collection.

While Chen Guiliang was chatting, his maternal grandparents' neighbors came over upon hearing the news.

More and more people gathered, all showering him with compliments.

There were also a few women who tried to ask indirectly if Chen Guiliang's company was hiring. They didn't have high hopes, just wanting to find jobs like security guard, cleaner, or mover for their children and grandchildren.

Chen Guiliang told them the truth, explaining what an office building was and that the security and cleaning were arranged by the property management company.

The villagers were a bit disappointed, but their attitude remained enthusiastic, figuring they might be able to ask Chen Guiliang for help someday.

"Beep! Beep! Beep!"

A motorcycle horn sounded from the village road.

It was Luo Xiaofen, who had received a call from her son and came to pick him up on her newly bought Jialing motorcycle.

"Grandpa, Grandma, Young Uncle, Aunt, I'll be leaving now."

"Stay for dinner before you go."

"My dad's here."

Chen Guiliang reached out to pinch the little girl's cheek. "Cousin, goodbye."

The little girl was shy and hid behind her young uncle. Seeing her actions, she seemed quite close to her stepfather.

Carrying the gifts he bought for his parents and grandmother, Chen Guiliang walked to the side of the village road, surrounded by the villagers.

Seeing his father's appearance, Chen Guiliang couldn't help but tease, "Whoa, are you acting in The Terminator?"

Luo Xiaofen was wearing a button-up shirt on top and colorful beach shorts below. What was even more ridiculous was that he was also wearing a pair of sunglasses, straddling a brand-new Jialing motorcycle.

Quite trendy and fashionable.

He was like a completely different person from the migrant worker he had been last year.

Parents also have their own pursuits and dreams. It was likely his father had wanted to do this for a long time.

It was very possible that when he was working in Yangcheng, he had envied others who could dress and relax like this. Now that his son was a tycoon and the family wasn't short on money, Luo Xiaofen could finally fulfill a dream he once had.

"Get on!"

Luo Xiaofen patted the back seat of the motorcycle and yelled at his son with great flair.
